sources.title: Kilkenny Timber Sale HI-720 — Specified Road Drawings and Engineers Estimate
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Hiawatha National Forest
sources.jurisdiction: United States; Michigan; Hiawatha National Forest East Zone
sources.cost_year_basis: Estimate sheet date; a separate underlying price survey/index base is not stated.
sources.scope: Reconstruction and localized improvements to 10 existing specified road segments: light grading, turnarounds, berms, selected aggregate placements. This is not a full new-road construction estimate.
sources.materials_basis: Supe Pit government-source Aggregate 23A and pit run; rates accompany hauled-and-placed construction schedules.
notes: Aggregate 23A item includes a USD7/CY processing fee paid to the Forest Service, conditional on permission to use the government source. This is not a retail aggregate supply quote.
Compaction is by operating hauling/spreading equipment across the full width.
Quantities are identified as loose hauled volume. Note 11 uses ambiguous '125% above compacted volume' wording; no compacted-volume conversion should be assumed.

Detailed schedule comments contain a stale USD1,400/14-roads mobilization statement. The estimate and quantity summary consistently allocate 10 × USD150 = USD1,500; use the estimate total and preserve the discrepancy.
The cover's road reconstruction lengths and the 1.32-mile grading quantity do not provide one unambiguous full-project length denominator; do not calculate an overall road USD/km benchmark.

sources.scope: Temporary forest roads and their eventual obliteration; separately, winter road maintenance. The temporary-road allowance includes drainage dips and one 18-inch CMP allowance. No aggregate surfacing or bridge cost is shown in the selected sheet.

classification.secondary: Access to multiple operations; 20–80 heavy vehicles per day; intermittent use.

No explicit tax, contingency, overhead or profit breakdown.

sources.title: Evaluation of Subgrade Stabilisation Methods for Upgrading Historic Forest Roads
sources.publisher: Forest Growers Research; Forest Engineering Honours Project with Port Blakely trial support
sources.upload_date_context: URL hosted under February 2025; report itself is a 2024 project.
sources.geography: Diamond Hill Road, Herbert Forest, and Bridgeman Road, Geraldine Forest, New Zealand
sources.locator: Methods: printed pages 22–26; Table 2 printed page 26 / PDF page 28; Table 3 printed page 27 / PDF page 29; Table 4 printed page 29 / PDF page 31; performance discussion printed pages 30–32.
sources.scope: Reconstruction of existing historic road subgrades using lime stabilisation, geogrid or undercut. Costs normalized to a 4.5 m road width and extrapolated per kilometre.
sources.method: Contractors measured machine time using hour clocks. Port Blakely supplied representative machine hourly rates. Material costs came from invoices. Total section costs were normalized to a common width and extrapolated to NZD/km.
sources.tax_basis: Excludes GST. Table 2 explicitly labels inputs excl. GST and Table 4 explicitly labels normalized costs excl. GST; Table 3 uses the same input-cost basis.

scopes.undercut: Remove unsuitable material to a suitable bearing layer, backfill with base material, grade and compact; excavation depth varied with site.
scopes.geogrid: Remove approximately 150 mm; place a 3.8 m wide strip of TriAX TX160 geogrid and approximately 150 mm base material; grade and compact.
scopes.lime: Remove approximately 250 mm, rip approximately 150 mm below this, incorporate 3% hydrated lime, replace approximately 250 mm base material and compact.

performance_context: The cheapest method was not necessarily the method meeting the strength target.
At Diamond Hill, wet-state CBR for geogrid was 15.04%, below the 30% design target; lime and undercut exceeded 30%.
At Bridgeman, none met 30% in the wettest condition; lime was 28.04% and undercut 29.75%.

The geogrid trials used readily available unscreened/ungraded aggregate instead of the manufacturer's recommended AP40, and vehicle movements were limited; the trial does not establish that geogrid is universally unsuitable.
exclusions_or_unknowns: These are normalized experimental reconstruction costs, not whole new-road construction or paid lump-sum contract prices.
No separately stated planning, mobilization, engineering, contingency, profit or overhead allowance.
Contractors were familiar with undercut but less familiar with the alternative methods.
Four-month monitoring does not establish life-cycle performance.
useful_model_features: Separate rock supply from truck delivery
Normalize by both width and length
Compare costs only among treatments meeting required service performance
Sensitivity to material price and site-specific excavation

sources.title: New Zealand Forest Road Engineering Manual, section 5.9: Estimating machinery production
sources.date: Live manual reviewed 2026-11-12; no artificial cost base assigned.
method: Estimate production using detailed records of actual past operations, at machine level where possible.
Compare actual production with the estimate and maintain the historical record.
Adjust for soil/rock, weather, operator, digging conditions, swing, obstructions and working space; similar roads can have different costs.
Excavator production depends on cycle frequency and average bucket payload.
Use explicit volume state (in-place versus loose), swell, equipment production, hourly charge including operator, transport cost and job-condition factors.
Manufacturer curves are fallback evidence and may not reflect current machines or the local operator.
sources.pgmaps_inference: A locally calibrated machine-hours × charge-rate model can explain why costs change. Use bank/loose/compacted volumes consistently and price mobilization separately.

sources.title: Putting a value on the benefits of forestry — Scion Forest Investment Framework application in Hawke's Bay
sources.publisher: New Zealand Ministry for Primary Industries / Canopy; Scion study
sources.method: Scion's Forest Investment Framework assigns spatial road costs by slope (0–5°, 5–15°, >15°) and erosion susceptibility; landing costs depend on slope and soil. This is an economic afforestation model, not a measured project bill of quantities.
sources.excluded_numeric_reason: The public summary's road-cost table labels dollar values but does not state the denominator. Do not ingest its figures as NZD/km without checking the underlying technical report.
sources.pgmaps_inference: Terrain classes can support a first-pass spatial screen, followed by site quantities, haul distances and drainage design for a route estimate.
